Every repository's CI and deployments on one screen, and no more text spilling out of the window.

### CI/CD across all your repositories (⌘6)

- A new **CI/CD** view lists every repository on this Mac (and your recent ones), failing first, then running, passing, and those without CI.
- Each row shows the latest checks on the default branch and, when you're on another branch, that branch too: "1 of 6 failed", "2 of 4 running", "6 passed".
- It reads everything that reports to GitHub, not just GitHub Actions: Buildkite, CircleCI, Vercel and other commit statuses show up alongside your workflows.
- **Deployments**: the latest deployment to each environment, with a link to the live site or the deploy log. A failed deployment marks the repository as failing.
- Select a repository to see all its checks; click one to open it on GitHub, or **Open in Actions** to jump to that repository's runs and logs.
- Filter by Failing / Running / Passing or by name. The sidebar shows how many repositories are failing.
- It refreshes every minute, and every 15 seconds while something is running. One request covers 20 repositories, so it stays well within GitHub's limits.

### Fixes

- **Title bar**: long repository names, worktree paths and branch names no longer wrap out of the bar; they end in an ellipsis, and the toolbar keeps its spacing in a narrow window.
- **Full text on hover**: anything cut off with an ellipsis shows its full text when you hover over it: commit messages and authors in History, run, job and step names in Actions, pull request commits and checks, stashes, repositories and paths on the Welcome screen, palette items, file paths and more.

### Install

Download the file for your system below. The builds are not signed with a paid certificate yet: on macOS right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time (or run `xattr -cr "/Applications/Git Graph.app"`); on Windows choose **More info → Run anyway**. Pull requests, Actions and CI/CD use the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) sign-in (`gh auth login`).
